item.title: Compositional Automata Learning of Timed Synchronous Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.21237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active model learning is a crucial technique for automatically constructing formal models of black-box timed systems. However, existing learning approaches typically construct a single monolithic automaton for a timed system with multiple synchronous components, obscuring its component structure and hindering component-level analysis. We propose a compositional learning approach that constructs a deterministic real-time automaton (RTA) for each component with access only to the target system as a whole. Upon termination, the learned RTAs form a network that exhibits exactly the same timed behaviors as the target system. Within the respective resource limits, our implementation terminates successfully on 213 of the 240 (88.8%) randomly generated benchmark instances and all six adapted case-study benchmarks, and requires less learning time than monolithic approaches on some instances.
item.dc:creator: Hanyue Chen, Chang Liu, Miaomiao Zhang

item.title: Model Checking HyperRecHML is Decidable
item.description: arXiv:2610.21379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Temporal hyperlogics combine explicit quantification over traces with temporal requirements evaluated over the quantified traces. HyperRecHML is a temporal hyperlogic which allows for arbitrary mixing of trace quantification and the use of fixed points for expressing temporal requirements, which makes it very expressive in comparison to other first-order hyperlogics. HyperRecHML has already been successfully applied in runtime verification, but the decidability of its model checking problem remains open. We answer this question positively by providing two main contributions. Firstly, a normalization procedure that allows to reduce arbitrary HyperRecHML formulas to a normal form with restricted nesting of trace quantification and fixed points. Secondly, we provide an automata-based model checking algorithm for formulas of this normal form. The complexity of our algorithm is comparable to similar ones for other hyperlogics, despite the extra expressive power.
item.dc:creator: Elli Anastasiadi, Kim Guldstrand Larsen, Martin Zimmermann

item.title: The complexity of smooth words over binary alphabets
item.description: arXiv:2603.10733v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Smooth sequences over an alphabet of positive integers $\{a,b\}$ are sequences that are infinitely derivable, the emblematic example being the Oldenburger-Kolakoski sequence $\kappa$ over $\{1,2\}$. The main way to study their language is to consider a finite version of smooth sequences called smooth words. In this paper we prove that the smooth words are exactly the factors of smooth sequences and we make progress towards the conjecture that the complexity of smooth words over $\{a,b\}$ grows like $\Theta\left(n^{\log(a+b)/\log((a+b)/2)}\right)$: we prove the lower bound over any alphabet and the upper bound over even alphabets, and we improve the known upper bound over odd and mixed alphabets. We also provide a dichotomy that links the language, the morphicity and the factor complexity of $\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Julien Cassaigne, Rapha\"el Henry

item.title: Polygraphic resolutions for operated algebras
item.description: arXiv:2502.16304v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper introduces the structure of operated polygraphs as a categorical model for rewriting in operated algebras, generalizing Gr\"obner--Shirshov bases with non-monomial termination orders. We show how to construct polygraphic resolutions of free operated algebras from confluent and terminating presentations. We provide a combinatorial description of critical branchings of operated polygraphs using the structure of polyautomata introduced in this paper. Polyautomata are linear polygraphs equipped with an operator structure formalized by a pushdown automaton. Finally, we apply our constructions to several families of operated algebras, including Rota--Baxter algebras, differential algebras, and differential Rota--Baxter algebras.
item.dc:creator: Zuan Liu, Philippe Malbos
